slides.heading: Zika Virus
slides.subtitle: A mosquito-borne flavivirus — usually mild, but dangerous in pregnancy.

slides.heading: Overview
bullets: Vectors: Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus.
Transmission: mosquito bite, congenital/intrauterine, perinatal, breastfeeding, sex, transfusion (platelet).

terms.definition: Extreme joint pain, particularly in hands and feet.

slides.heading: Other Features
bullets: Other symptoms: edema, headache, lymphadenopathy, myalgia, retro-orbital pain, vomiting.
Diagnosis: PCR / Zika virus nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT).

slides.heading: Pregnancy Risks & DOH Guidelines
bullets: Congenital Zika Syndrome — brain defect (microcephaly), miscarriage, stillbirth, other birth defects.
Immediate OB-GYN referral if a pregnant woman has rash, fever, or red eyes.
Serial ultrasounds to monitor fetal development; counseling; refer high-risk pregnancies to tertiary hospitals.

slides.heading: Treatment (Symptomatic — No Specific Cure)
bullets: Paracetamol for fever and body aches; AVOID NSAIDs (ibuprofen, aspirin).
Prevention: 4 S's, repellents (DEET, Picaridin), nets, fogging, biologic vector control.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Zika = flavivirus; conjunctivitis distinguishes it from dengue/chikungunya.
Major danger is in pregnancy → microcephaly (Congenital Zika Syndrome).
Also spreads sexually, perinatally, and via transfusion.
